Pikeliai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Telšiai County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Pikeliai grew to two-thirds Jewish by 1897, though the formal marking of the Lithuania-Latvia border later cut off local Jewish traders from Latvian markets, seriously damaging their livelihoods; only about 150 families remained by 1914, and just 20 by 1940. In 1941, Pikeliai's Jews suffered abuse from their own Lithuanian neighbors even before their murder by Nazi forces and collaborators that August. The town produced an unusual concentration of notable descendants: American philanthropist brothers Robert and Albert Shif; Rabbi Eliyahu-David Rabinovitz-Teomim, who emigrated to Israel and was elected rabbi of Jerusalem — and whose son-in-law was Abraham Isaac Kook, the first Chief Rabbi of British Mandate Palestine and uncle of Hillel Kook, documented at a separate cemetery in Kriukai elsewhere in this collection.
